issues.detail: The Greek 'ζηλωτην' (zelous) is translated as 'sốt sắng' (fervent/zealous). While similar, in this specific context of the Gospels, 'ζηλωτής' often carries a connotation of being 'impetuous' or 'hot-tempered' rather than just 'fervent'. However, more critically, the Vietnamese 'gọi là người sốt sắng' (called a fervent person) lacks the nuance of the Greek construction where 'καλούμενον' is a participle modifying Simon. The Vietnamese phrasing makes it sound like a title or a general description, whereas the Greek identifies him as 'Simon the Zealot'.
